title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Trident Labs
summary: Initial discovery for Trident Labs evaluating Redwood's hosted API with potential roadmap to Dedicated or Private. Key asks: time-to-first-token, free credits/quickstart, data residency, SOC 2 compliance, KMS support, latency vs cost tradeoffs. Agreed to pilot with free credits + technical demo; Redwood to share pricing and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Marisol Reyes, Ben Carter, Sofia Kim (Trident Labs)

[00:00:05] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joined by Priya who's our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Marisol Reyes: Doing well, thanks. Quick background - we're Trident Labs, building a customer support assistant for enterprise SaaS, evaluating inference providers.
[00:00:20] Alex Chen: Great, that's exactly what we help with. Today we wanted to understand your constraints and timeline, show how fast you can get started with Redwood PLG quickstart - free credits, SDKs, and typical time-to-first-token, and then map to Dedicated or Private if needed.
[00:00:35] Sofia Kim: We're trying to get something in production in Q2, ideally within 6-8 weeks, so time-to-value is big.
[00:00:42] Priya Nair: Totally - that timeline makes sense. For PLG/self-serve people usually spin up hosted API, use our quickstart, we give trial credits. Typical time-to-first-token for devs is under an hour if you follow the quickstart and have your prompts ready; we've seen teams get a basic integration in 15-30 minutes.
[00:01:00] Ben Carter: Nice - what does the quickstart include? Is there a sandbox model or...
[00:01:06] Alex Chen: We provide a starter repo, sample prompts, and 200 USD in free credits for trials by default; we can increase that for pilots. There are curated open-model variants and small development tiers so you can iterate without high costs.
[00:01:20] Marisol Reyes: On security - we're handling customer data, regulated verticals, need SOC 2, data residency in EU, KMS for keys. Can hosted support those?
[00:01:30] Priya Nair: Short answer: yes. Our hosted API is SOC 2 compliant; we have European regions, and support customer-managed keys via KMS integration for Private and Dedicated - hosted can also integrate with KMS for enterprise plans, and we log requests for audit. We'll send the SOC 2 report and security whitepaper after the call.
[00:01:50] Sofia Kim: For data residency if we start with hosted in the EU, is data kept there?
[00:01:56] Priya Nair: Yes our EU region keeps data in-region; there are retention and logging policies you can configure. If you need full control or air-gapped, Private on a VPC/on-prem is the option.
[00:02:10] Ben Carter: Performance-wise, for the assistant we need p50 latency under 200ms for short prompts, and high throughput at peak. How does that map to hosted vs dedicated?
[00:02:20] Priya Nair: Hosted can hit low latencies for medium-sized models, but for consistent p50/p95 under tight SLOs Dedicated is better - reserved GPU pools with autoscaling. We also have model variants and quantization profiles that reduce latency and cost. We can run benchmarks against your prompt set as part of a pilot.
[00:02:40] Marisol Reyes: Costs are a big concern - what levers do we have?
[00:02:45] Alex Chen: A few levers: batching and KV caching reduce per-token cost; choosing quantized models or smaller model variants lowers unit cost; dedicated reserved capacity reduces variability and usually lowers $/token at scale. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations automatically.
[00:03:05] Ben Carter: If we go hosted and later move to Dedicated, is the API compatible?
[00:03:10] Alex Chen: Yes - same API across modes, same SDKs. Rollouts and model pinning work across hosted, dedicated, private. You can start hosted and lift-and-shift to Dedicated with minimal changes.
[00:03:20] Sofia Kim: Any gotchas around KV cache behavior or streaming responses for chat?
[00:03:25] Priya Nair: We support streaming and KV cache; for long-lived conversations we expose controls for cache lifetime and prefix caching. There are nuances with tokenization and prompt truncation we'll help tune during POC.
[00:03:40] Marisol Reyes: About the trial credits, you mentioned 200 USD by default - can we get more to run a proper benchmark?
[00:03:47] Alex Chen: Absolutely - for pilots we typically provision larger credits and run a benchmark plan. We'll need a short scope (prompt set, target qps) and we'll run end-to-end tests.
[00:03:58] Ben Carter: What's the usual timeline for a pilot benchmark?
[00:04:02] Priya Nair: Usually a week for setup + run, depending on workload. We can do a lightweight smoke test in 1-2 days to validate integration and then schedule full run.
[00:04:12] Sofia Kim: Who will be the point of contact for security questions?
[00:04:15] Alex Chen: I'll send the security pack and intro you to our security engineer. Priya will run the technical demo and benchmarks.
[00:04:25] Marisol Reyes: One more - SSO and RBAC for teams is important.
[00:04:29] Priya Nair: We support SAML SSO, granular RBAC, audit logs. For Dedicated/Private you can map to your IdP and get full control.
[00:04:38] Ben Carter: How do you handle fallbacks if capacity is constrained? We can't have our assistant go down.
[00:04:44] Priya Nair: Built-in smart routing: requests can fallback to compatible model variants or other regions, and you can set policy per route. For critical flows we recommend canary/fallback policies and dedicated capacity as a safety net.
[00:04:58] Sofia Kim: OK - success criteria for us would be: reliable latency under target, security signoff, and cost predictability.
[00:05:05] Alex Chen: Makes sense. Proposed next steps: we'll provision pilot credits, share quickstart link and starter repo, send security docs and SOC 2, and schedule a 60-minute technical demo with Priya to walk through integration and run a smoke test.
[00:05:20] Marisol Reyes: Sounds good. Also can you send estimated pricing ranges for hosted vs dedicated?
[00:05:25] Alex Chen: Yes I'll send a pricing sheet with ballpark $/token and reserved capacity estimates.
[00:05:30] Ben Carter: For the smoke test, I'll provide a sample prompt set and target QPS.
[00:05:34] Alex Chen: Perfect.
[00:05:40] -- small talk and wrap up --
[00:06:00] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.

Transcript notes: transcription quality medium - occasional speaker mis-attribution and small ASR errors (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed correctly but proper nouns sometimes off).
